records.learning_takeaway: Connect an Egyptian board race with New Kingdom beliefs about the afterlife.
records.card: Senet used a thirty-square board in ancient Egypt. Its imagery became more than decoration: during the New Kingdom, the game's passage through marked hazards was associated with the deceased person's journey toward the afterlife. Surviving game boxes connect recreation with funerary belief.

records.label: Sensory adaptation
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish continuing sensory stimulation from reduced conscious notice over time.
records.card: With prolonged stimulation, a continuing sensory input can become less noticeable even while it remains present. OpenStax describes this as sensory adaptation. The change highlights a gap between continuing stimulation and conscious experience, helping explain why an initially prominent feature of the surroundings can fade from awareness.

records.label: Separation of privilege
records.learning_takeaway: Require independently held authorities so one error or compromised party cannot alone unlock a protected action.
records.card: Separation of privilege requires more than one independent authority for a protected action. Splitting the necessary keys between different people, programs, or organizations means a single accident or breach need not suffice. It is different from merely assigning one powerful user a more complicated password.

records.label: Sestina: Altaforte
records.learning_takeaway: Pound adopts a troubadour-warrior’s voice and recurring end-words; an editorial reading hears their repetition intensifying the monologue’s praise of combat.
records.card: In Sestina: Altaforte, Ezra Pound adopts the voice of a troubadour-warrior praising combat. The poem’s end-words recur in changing contexts. An editorial reading hears that recurrence intensifying the speaker’s fervor, while keeping the dramatic persona distinct from the poet.

records.label: Sexual cannibalism in redback spiders
records.learning_takeaway: Explore why a mating behavior that risks death can still correlate with increased paternity.
records.card: In laboratory redback-spider observations, second males that were cannibalized mated longer, and longer mating was associated with more paternity. This offers a possible reproductive explanation for a behavior that risks death. The evidence concerns a small experimental sample, not a guaranteed outcome for every male.

records.label: Sexual selection
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish mating success from survival when explaining conspicuous or risky traits.
records.card: A trait can improve success in obtaining mates while making survival harder. Sexual selection explains why conspicuous ornaments or risky mating behavior can spread despite such costs. The relevant outcome is contribution to the next generation, not simply how long an individual stays alive.

records.label: Shabad
records.learning_takeaway: Sung or recited Sikh hymns are understood as divine teaching, joining scriptural words with everyday devotion.
records.card: A shabad is a Sikh hymn sung or recited as a source of guidance and inspiration. Hymns from the Guru Granth Sahib are understood as divine teaching. Their use in worship and ordinary life connects the scripture’s words with memory, sound and repeated devotional practice.

records.label: Sharpening burr
records.learning_takeaway: Recognize the fragile wire edge left by sharpening and why it must be removed from a finished cutting edge.
records.card: Sharpening a blade can leave a thin wire edge, or burr, along the cutting edge. An unwanted burr may feel sharp initially but break away during use, leaving a rougher edge. Honing removes this fragile remnant, so forming an edge and finishing it are distinct parts of sharpening.

records.label: Shibam
records.learning_takeaway: Tall mud-brick houses combine dense defensive settlement with the floodplain resources that supplied agriculture and building material.
records.card: Shibam’s tall mud-brick houses concentrate urban life within a compact defensive settlement. The surrounding floodplain supplied agricultural resources and building material. Its architecture is therefore tied to the landscape beyond the walls, combining dense habitation with dependence on nearby water and land.

records.label: Shogi impasse
records.learning_takeaway: Explore material counting when neither advanced king can plausibly be mated.
records.card: Under the cited professional shogi impasse procedure, both kings have entered enemy territory and neither mating prospects nor further captures remain. Rooks and bishops count five points; other nonking pieces count one. Both players having at least twenty-four points leads to a draw and replay.

records.label: Signal detection theory
records.learning_takeaway: Explore detecting a target among noise when expectations and task goals influence reports.
records.card: Signal detection theory separates sensory evidence from the criterion for reporting a signal. With evidence quality held fixed, lowering the criterion can increase both hits and false alarms; raising it can reduce both. Better sensitivity and greater willingness to answer yes are different changes.

records.label: Signed social network
records.learning_takeaway: Represent both friendly and antagonistic relations with edge signs instead of recording only whether a relationship exists.
records.card: A signed social network records whether a relationship is positive or negative, rather than only whether a tie exists. This allows friendship and antagonism to appear in the same representation. Researchers can then examine configurations such as shared enemies or incompatible alliances, while recognizing that two signs simplify richer relationships.

records.label: Silicon passivation
records.learning_takeaway: A thin oxide layer protects silicon; removing that layer changes its chemical reactivity.
records.card: Silicon can protect itself with a thin surface layer of silicon dioxide. This passivation changes how the underlying material reacts with its surroundings. When hot, strong aqueous base removes the oxide, exposed silicon can react, illustrating the importance of surface chemistry to bulk behavior.

records.label: Simultaneous contrast
records.learning_takeaway: A color can look different because of the colors immediately surrounding it.
records.card: Simultaneous contrast occurs when a color’s appearance changes with the colors beside it. The same painted area may therefore seem different in another setting. Comparing adjacent combinations shows that color is perceived relationally, rather than as an isolated property experienced identically in every composition.

records.label: Singulative narration
records.learning_takeaway: A telling can represent one occurrence once, providing the baseline relation against which other narrative frequencies are compared.
records.card: Singulative narration tells once what happened once. Its defining feature is the relation between occurrences and tellings, not the length of the passage. A long account can still be singulative if it represents a single occurrence one time.

records.label: Situational superko
records.learning_takeaway: Compare a whole-game repetition ban with the immediate ko restriction.
records.card: Under the British Go Association's AGA-style rule, a player cannot make a play that recreates a board position previously created by that player. This reaches beyond immediate ko recapture, preventing longer repeating cycles such as triple ko from continuing indefinitely.

records.label: Skin grafting
records.learning_takeaway: Explain why transferred skin must acquire blood supply from its new wound bed.
records.card: A skin graft moves a piece of detached skin onto a wound that needs coverage. For the graft to survive, it must gain a blood supply from the receiving area. Successful placement therefore depends on biological attachment and nourishment, not merely covering the wound’s surface.

records.label: Skin pigmentation and pulse oximetry
records.learning_takeaway: Recognize skin pigmentation as one factor that can make an optical oxygen estimate inaccurate.
records.card: Pulse oximeters estimate oxygen saturation using light, and skin pigmentation is one factor that can affect the result. A displayed number should therefore not be treated as equally exact in every person or circumstance. Understanding this limitation separates a convenient estimate from an infallible measurement.

records.label: Slow-slip events
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish prolonged transient fault slip from the rapid rupture of ordinary earthquakes.
records.card: Not all fault slip occurs as a sudden earthquake rupture. In Cascadia, slow-slip events produce deformation over longer periods and are observed through precise position measurements together with unusual seismic signals. They reveal movement on the plate boundary that the ordinary locked-then-breaking picture leaves incomplete.

records.label: S–N curve
records.learning_takeaway: Relate cyclic stress amplitude to measured fatigue life, recognizing that not every material has an endurance limit.
records.card: An S–N curve links repeated stress amplitude with the number of cycles a test specimen survives before failure. Some materials show an endurance-limit plateau, while others do not. Reading the curve requires the loading conditions, so one fatigue-life value cannot describe every service situation.

records.label: Snapshot isolation
records.learning_takeaway: Give a read transaction a stable historical view while later commits remain invisible until it restarts.
records.card: Snapshot isolation gives a transaction a stable view of data while other transactions may commit changes. SQLite's WAL readers keep seeing their earlier snapshot until they start a new transaction. A stable snapshot describes visibility; by itself, that description does not establish every system's serializability guarantees.

records.label: Social desirability bias
records.learning_takeaway: Consider why answers about behavior may reflect a wish to appear acceptable.
records.card: Social desirability bias can make self-reports reflect how people want to appear rather than what they actually do or believe. A respondent might underreport drinking to seem more acceptable. This is one possible source of inaccurate survey answers, alongside memory errors and other influences.

records.label: Social norms
records.learning_takeaway: Recognize shared expectations for conduct, including unwritten rules learned by observing others and their consequences.
records.card: Social norms are shared expectations about conduct. Some are written and formally enforced, while others are learned through observation and everyday reactions. A person's behavior can follow a norm even without an official watching, because approval, disapproval, and anticipated consequences also help sustain expectations.

records.label: Sociolinguistic corpus
records.learning_takeaway: Combine recordings across a relevant speaker sample so community patterns can be distinguished from individual habits.
records.card: A sociolinguistic corpus brings together records of language use so patterns can be studied beyond one person's conversation. Collections may include interviews, letters, or other speech and writing. Which speakers and contexts are represented matters when interpreting a pattern as characteristic of a wider community.

records.label: Sociolinguistic interview
records.learning_takeaway: Compare speech across tasks that elicit different levels of self-monitoring, or collect natural conversation.
records.card: A sociolinguistic interview gathers speech for studying variation. Tasks such as reading passages, pronouncing word pairs, and casual conversation can elicit different levels of self-monitoring. Researchers tailor the format to their question; an interview seeking natural conversation need not use every traditional task.

records.label: Sogdian merchant diasporas
records.learning_takeaway: Sogdian commercial communities also transmitted religious traditions, artistic practices and languages through their dispersed trading networks.
records.card: Sogdian merchants established communities along Eurasian trade networks rather than merely passing through them. These dispersed settlements helped goods, languages, religions and artistic practices circulate. Their history shows how sustained social connections could make merchants influential cultural intermediaries.

records.label: Soil liquefaction
records.learning_takeaway: Explain how shaking can make loose water-saturated sediment lose supporting strength.
records.card: Strong shaking can make loose, water-saturated sediment lose much of its supporting strength. During soil liquefaction, ground that previously carried buildings or other loads can deform and fail. The hazard depends on the material and water conditions, not just the earthquake’s size.

records.label: Soil tensiometer
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish how tightly soil holds water from the amount of water it contains.
records.card: A soil tensiometer uses a water-filled tube, a porous ceramic tip and a gauge to assess soil-water tension. It measures how tightly the soil holds water, not simply the fraction of soil volume occupied by water. That distinction matters when judging how hard roots must work to extract moisture.

records.label: Sonatas and Interludes
records.learning_takeaway: Connect a particular Cage cycle with reproducible preparations altering piano sound.
records.card: Cage's Sonatas and Interludes, composed in 1946–48, uses a prepared piano whose strings are altered by inserted materials. The John Cage Trust later supervised samples made with the work's actual preparation materials, linking the composition's identity to a particular physically modified sound source.

records.label: Song scholar-officials
records.learning_takeaway: Literary education and service linked elite prestige with duties that could include criticizing rulers’ policies.
records.card: Song scholar-officials joined literary cultivation with government service. Their education helped define elite status, while their duties could include criticizing a ruler’s conduct. The role therefore linked political participation with a learned ideal of responsibility that could place officials in tension with authority.

records.label: Sorites paradox
records.learning_takeaway: See how apparently harmless small changes can generate a contradiction about vague categories.
records.card: The sorites paradox turns tiny changes into a puzzle about vague categories. If one grain is not a heap, and adding one grain never makes the difference, repeated additions seem to imply that no heap is possible. Plausible small steps produce an unacceptable conclusion.

records.label: South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission
records.learning_takeaway: Compare truth-finding, reparations and amnesty as separate parts of a post-apartheid process.
records.card: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission addressed abuses associated with apartheid through separate work on human-rights violations, reparations and rehabilitation, and amnesty. Its committee structure shows that truth-finding, assistance to victims and decisions about perpetrators' amnesty were related tasks, rather than one undifferentiated act of forgiveness.

records.label: South Sea Bubble
records.learning_takeaway: Examine how national-debt conversion and expectations drove a company's stock boom despite limited trading activity.
records.card: The South Sea Bubble linked speculation in company shares with British government debt. The Bank of England's history describes limited trading but a dramatic stock-price rise after the company received part of the national debt in 1720. The episode contrasts share prices with actual trading activity.
records.primary_subfield: Economic history and documented business cases

records.label: Span of control
records.learning_takeaway: Choose how many people report directly to a manager, affecting oversight and the number of hierarchy layers.
records.card: Span of control concerns how many people report directly to a manager. A narrow span gives each manager fewer direct reports and can accompany more layers of hierarchy. Choosing the span is therefore part of balancing supervision and coordination, not simply choosing an impressive management title.

records.label: Spanning tree
records.learning_takeaway: A connected graph can be reduced to a cycle-free set of edges that still reaches every vertex.
records.card: A spanning tree keeps every vertex of a finite connected graph while using just enough edges to preserve connectivity without cycles. For n vertices it has n minus one edges. Different choices can connect the same graph, so a network may have many spanning trees.

records.label: Spatial autocorrelation
records.learning_takeaway: Nearby locations can have similar or dissimilar measured values; testing the pattern uses both attributes and spatial relationships.
records.card: Spatial autocorrelation asks whether nearby places tend to have similar or dissimilar measured values. A test combines the values with a definition of spatial relationships. It can distinguish clustering, dispersion or an absence of detected pattern, without by itself explaining what caused the arrangement.

records.label: Species counterpoint
records.learning_takeaway: Learn how controlled note ratios organize practice in combining independent melodies.
records.card: Species counterpoint teaches melodic combination through restricted rhythmic relationships. Exercises can place one, two, three or four notes against a note in another voice. The cited textbook focuses on two voices, while noting that a longer college course may extend the method to four.

records.label: Specific impulse
records.learning_takeaway: Compare thrust per propellant weight-flow rate, rather than thrust alone, when evaluating rocket propulsion.
records.card: Specific impulse compares rocket thrust with propellant weight-flow rate, using standard gravity to convert from mass flow. Its units are seconds, but it is not the engine’s burn duration. A higher value means more impulse per unit propellant, rather than necessarily a larger thrust force.

records.label: Spirometry
records.learning_takeaway: Measure both the amount and speed of exhaled air to investigate lung function.
records.card: Spirometry records how much air a person can blow out and how quickly it leaves the lungs. A forceful breath into a measuring device produces information about airflow and volume. It is one part of lung-function assessment, rather than a single test that identifies every breathing disorder.

records.label: Spit bite aquatint
records.learning_takeaway: Applying acid directly with a brush to an aquatinted plate allows the printmaker to create wash-like tonal passages.
records.card: Spit bite aquatint applies acid directly with a brush to an aquatinted plate. The local treatment allows tonal passages that resemble washes rather than relying only on an evenly timed bath. The resulting printed marks connect painterly handling with an intaglio process.

records.label: Spitzer Space Telescope
records.learning_takeaway: Liquid-helium cooling suppressed the infrared telescope’s own heat during its original cryogenic mission.
records.card: Spitzer’s original cryogenic design cooled its telescope assembly to about five kelvin using liquid helium. Suppressing the observatory’s own infrared emission helped prevent its thermal glow from interfering with observations of relatively cold cosmic objects.

records.label: SQL
records.learning_takeaway: Describe desired query results declaratively while a database planner chooses how to find them.
records.card: SQL lets a program describe the data it wants rather than prescribe every retrieval step. The database's query planner chooses an execution strategy, such as scanning a table or using an index. The same requested result can therefore be produced through different underlying algorithms.

records.label: SQLite
records.learning_takeaway: Embed a transactional database directly in an application without a separate database server process.
records.card: SQLite embeds a transactional SQL database engine inside an application. It reads and writes ordinary files without a separate database server process, and a complete database can occupy one file. That design makes a database library useful where an application would otherwise manage its own file format.

records.label: Stalemate
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish having no legal move from being checkmated.
records.card: Stalemate is a drawn chess position in which the player to move has no legal move and their king is not in check. The distinction from checkmate is crucial: immobilizing the opponent does not win if no attack on the king accompanies that immobilization.

records.label: Standing to sue
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish a concrete, redressable legal injury from disagreement with government policy.
records.card: In US federal court, standing ordinarily requires a concrete, particularized injury that is actual or imminent, linked to the challenged conduct and likely to be redressed by a favorable decision. Disagreeing with a policy is therefore different from showing the personal stake needed to bring the lawsuit.

records.label: Starch gelatinization
records.learning_takeaway: Explain thickening when starch granules absorb water and swell during heating.
records.card: When starch is heated with water, its granules absorb water and swell, thickening the mixture. This gelatinization helps give sauces and puddings their texture. It is a change in the hydrated starch structure, distinct from simply dissolving a sweetener or cooling a gelatin dessert.

records.label: Starch retrogradation
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish molecular re-ordering during storage from the initial swelling of starch during cooking.
records.card: After starch has been cooked, its molecules can associate again and develop more ordered structures during storage. This retrogradation changes the starch matrix and can affect texture and digestibility. It is a later rearrangement, distinct from the initial water uptake and swelling of heated starch granules.

records.label: Stare decisis
records.learning_takeaway: Compare following a higher court with following one's own prior decisions.
records.card: Stare decisis promotes consistency by directing courts to follow precedent. In the cited US account, vertical precedent comes from higher courts; horizontal precedent concerns a court's own earlier decisions. The Supreme Court can overrule its precedents, so continuity does not make every prior ruling permanent.

records.label: Staystitching
records.learning_takeaway: Stabilize an individual cut fabric edge before handling and assembly stretch it out of shape.
records.card: Staystitching adds a permanent row of stitches to an individual fabric piece before assembly. Placed within the seam allowance, it helps keep vulnerable curves or bias edges from stretching during handling. It stabilizes the cut shape, rather than serving as the seam that joins two pieces together.

records.label: Steam bending
records.learning_takeaway: Use heat and moisture to soften wood, then retain a curved shape while it cools and dries.
records.card: Steam bending uses heat and moisture to make suitable wood more flexible. The piece is shaped and then restrained while it cools and dries, helping it retain the curve. Moisture changes later can still alter that shape, so bending success involves both forming and conditioning the material.

records.label: Stellar parallax
records.learning_takeaway: Earth’s orbital baseline turns tiny annual angular shifts into geometric stellar-distance measurements.
records.card: Stellar parallax measures distance from a star’s apparent shift as Earth changes position in its orbit. Nearby stars shift more than distant ones against the background. Knowing the observing baseline turns this tiny angular change into a geometric measurement rather than an estimate based on stellar brightness.

records.label: Stellar proper motion
records.learning_takeaway: Separate stars’ long-term angular motion from line-of-sight velocity to reconstruct motion through space.
records.card: Proper motion is a star’s persistent angular drift across the sky over time. It differs from motion toward or away from us measured by radial velocity. Combining proper motion, distance, and radial velocity lets astronomers reconstruct the star’s actual movement through space.

records.label: Stereographic projection
records.learning_takeaway: Project from a sphere’s pole onto a plane to translate spherical locations into planar coordinates.
records.card: Stereographic projection maps a sphere, apart from its projection pole, onto a plane. Draw a line from the pole through a surface point and continue it to the plane. The construction turns spherical positions into planar coordinates using the geometry of similar triangles.

records.label: Stern–Gerlach experiment
records.learning_takeaway: A nonuniform magnetic field splits a silver-atom beam into two bands rather than a classical continuum.
records.card: The Stern–Gerlach experiment sent ground-state silver atoms through a nonuniform magnetic field and produced two separated bands. A classical picture allowing every magnetic orientation would predict a continuous spread. The result reveals quantized angular-momentum projections associated with the atoms’ unpaired electron spin.

records.label: Stirling numbers of the second kind
records.learning_takeaway: Count partitions of a labeled set into a fixed number of nonempty unlabeled blocks.
records.card: Stirling numbers of the second kind count ways to divide distinct objects into a fixed number of nonempty, unlabeled groups. Three objects can form two groups in three ways. Membership matters, but swapping the order in which the groups are listed does not create another partition.

records.label: Story stick
records.learning_takeaway: Preserve project dimensions together on a physical reference rather than repeatedly translating separate numbers.
records.card: A story stick carries a project’s important dimensions as full-size marks on one physical strip. The marks preserve their relationship to one another and provide a reusable layout reference. Transferring those positions can reduce the need to repeatedly reinterpret a list of separate numerical measurements.

records.label: Stratified sortition for citizens’ assemblies
records.learning_takeaway: See how lottery recruitment and demographic stratification produce an intended mini-public.
records.card: Ireland's citizens' assembly recruitment combines chance with demographic balancing. Randomly invited households may nominate an adult applicant; members are then selected using demographic information so the group broadly resembles society. The resulting mini-public is intended to be diverse, rather than simply comprising whoever volunteers first.

records.label: Strawberry Thief
records.learning_takeaway: Morris used indigo-discharge printing for Strawberry Thief, a textile pattern inspired by fruit-stealing thrushes in his garden.
records.card: William Morris’s Strawberry Thief was produced using indigo-discharge printing. Its motif was inspired by thrushes stealing fruit in his garden. The V&A connects the method with crisp outlines, offering a technical context for examining the pattern’s printed detail.
records.primary_subfield: Works, movements and historical design cases

records.label: Stress intensity factor
records.learning_takeaway: Combine applied stress, crack size, and geometry to characterize loading near a crack tip.
records.card: A stress intensity factor describes the strength of an elastic crack-tip stress field. In opening mode, it depends on applied stress, crack size, and geometry. Two components carrying similar nominal stress can therefore face different crack-tip loading if their flaws differ in size or shape.

records.label: Stretch tuning
records.learning_takeaway: Explain slightly widened piano octaves through the inharmonicity of stiff strings.
records.card: Piano octaves are often tuned slightly wider than a strict two-to-one frequency ratio. Stiff strings have upper partials sharper than ideal harmonics. Matching the upper note to a lower string's second partial can reduce audible beating, making a mathematically exact octave a poor practical match.

records.label: Strong triadic closure property
records.learning_takeaway: Use an explicitly idealized rule that two strong neighbors must also have some tie to derive network consequences.
records.card: The strong triadic closure property is an idealized rule: if someone has strong ties to two others, those two must have at least some tie between them. It permits deductions about network structure. The source explicitly warns that real social networks need not satisfy this rule everywhere.

records.label: Structural ambiguity
records.learning_takeaway: Derive different interpretations from alternative phrase attachments while keeping the words unchanged.
records.card: Structural ambiguity occurs when the same words allow different internal groupings. In I saw someone with a telescope, the telescope may be the instrument used for seeing or something the other person possessed. The difference comes from phrase attachment, without requiring a word to acquire another meaning.

records.label: Structural balance in social networks
records.learning_takeaway: Model consistency of positive and negative ties by distinguishing balanced triangles from potentially conflicting configurations.
records.card: Structural balance studies patterns of friendly and antagonistic ties. In its basic signed-triangle model, triangles with one or three positive edges count as balanced. Other combinations represent proposed tensions, such as being friends with two people who dislike each other; the model simplifies real relationships deliberately.

records.label: Structural holes
records.learning_takeaway: Recognize opportunities for brokerage where otherwise weakly connected groups hold different information.
records.card: Structural holes are gaps between groups that do not otherwise interact closely. Someone whose connections span such a gap may obtain information from different circles or broker their contact. The position can offer opportunities, but it can also create conflicting expectations and incentives to preserve the gap.

records.label: Stupa
records.learning_takeaway: A structure housing sacred relics or texts provides a focus of Buddhist veneration, often approached through circumambulation.
records.card: A stupa is a Buddhist structure that can house sacred relics and texts and serve as a focus of veneration. Forms range from small objects to monuments. Moving around a stupa in circumambulation connects the physical structure with an embodied devotional practice.

records.label: Style shifting
records.learning_takeaway: Observe speakers changing variant frequencies with speaking context rather than assigning one fixed style to each class.
records.card: Style shifting is a change in how a speaker uses linguistic variants across situations. Labov's New York study compared casual speech with reading aloud and found systematic differences in variant frequencies. Such shifts show that describing someone's language with one unchanging social label misses variation within that person's usage.

records.label: Subak
records.learning_takeaway: Balinese farmer collectives coordinate irrigation across terraced watersheds through institutions centered on water temples.
records.card: Subak is a Balinese institution through which farmers coordinate irrigation and related obligations. Water temples connect these collective arrangements across terraced watersheds. The system joins agricultural management with ritual organization, showing how distributing water can depend on shared institutions as well as physical channels.

records.label: Suberogation
records.learning_takeaway: Consider the disputed category of bad yet morally permitted conduct.
records.card: Suberogation is a proposed category of morally bad but permissible conduct, conceived as a counterpart to good actions beyond duty. Ingratitude is sometimes offered as an example, but both the examples and the category are disputed. Badness and prohibited wrongdoing need not be treated as identical.

records.label: Successive contrast
records.learning_takeaway: An afterimage from a color seen first can alter the appearance of a color viewed afterward.
records.card: Successive contrast occurs when an afterimage from a previously viewed color affects the appearance of a color seen afterward. The relationship unfolds across time, rather than between neighboring patches viewed together. What the viewer has just looked at becomes part of the next color experience.

records.label: Sugar-lift etching
records.learning_takeaway: A water-soluble sugar drawing beneath a varnish ground lifts away in water, exposing drawn areas for etching, often after aquatint.
records.card: Sugar-lift etching begins with a water-soluble drawing that is covered by a resistant ground. Water dissolves the drawing and lifts the covering above it, exposing those areas for further work. The method lets drawn marks determine where the plate can subsequently be etched.

records.label: Summary judgment
records.learning_takeaway: Understand deciding a claim without trial when no material factual dispute requires resolution.
records.card: In US federal civil procedure, summary judgment can resolve a claim without trial when no genuine dispute of material fact remains and the moving party is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. It does not authorize choosing between competing evidence that a reasonable factfinder could resolve differently.

records.label: Sunset provision
records.learning_takeaway: Understand automatic expiration as a way to require renewed legislative approval.
records.card: A sunset provision makes a law, program or agency expire after a specified period unless renewed through the required legislative process. Instead of requiring a fresh decision to terminate it, the provision makes continuation depend on renewed approval. This changes the default when lawmakers take no action.

records.label: Supererogation
records.learning_takeaway: Explore the possibility of morally good actions that duty does not require.
records.card: Supererogation is morally good action beyond what duty requires. A costly rescue may be admired even when failing to undertake it would not violate an obligation. Whether such optional goodness forms a genuine category is disputed, because some ethical theories make every morally best action compulsory.

records.label: Supervaluationism
records.learning_takeaway: Explore evaluating a vague statement across admissible precise interpretations.
records.card: Supervaluationism evaluates a vague statement across admissible ways of making its terms precise. A statement true under every such interpretation is supertrue; some borderline statements are neither supertrue nor superfalse. This permits truth-value gaps while preserving many classical logical laws, including excluded middle.

records.label: Surface triangulation
records.learning_takeaway: Represent a surface by joined triangles so its topology can be studied combinatorially.
records.card: A surface triangulation represents a surface as triangles joined along compatible edges. This replaces an apparently continuous object with pieces that can be counted and assembled. The construction supports topological reasoning without requiring the triangles to preserve every original distance or angle.

records.label: Surrogate endpoint
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish a quickly measured biological indicator from a direct patient benefit.
records.card: A surrogate endpoint is a measured indicator used in place of an outcome that matters directly to patients. Tumor shrinkage, for example, can be observed sooner than longer survival. The substitution is useful only to the extent that the indicator reliably reflects the benefit being sought.

records.label: Suspension in tonal music
records.learning_takeaway: Trace preparation, accented dissonance and downward stepwise resolution.
records.card: A suspension carries a prepared note into a moment where it becomes an accented non-chord tone, then resolves downward by step. Its three stages are preparation, suspension and resolution. Labels such as 4–3 describe the changing interval above the bass rather than the note's absolute pitch.

records.label: Swarna-Sub1
records.learning_takeaway: See flood tolerance as a bounded crop trait rather than an ability to survive indefinitely underwater.
records.card: Swarna-Sub1 adds temporary flood tolerance to a widely grown rice variety through the SUB1 breeding trait. It can survive periods of submergence that threaten ordinary crops, but longer floods still pose serious limits. The case shows why a tolerant variety is not an invulnerable one.

records.label: Sweeping in curling
records.learning_takeaway: Explore altering stone travel through work on the ice rather than touching the stone.
records.card: World Curling's 2024 report describes sweepers using pressure, brush angle and technique to influence a stone's distance and curl. Athletes test methods on different ice surfaces and disagree about some effects. The account documents evolving practice rather than establishing that every reported technique works equally well.

records.label: Syneresis
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish water expelled by a contracting gel from water merely added to a food.
records.card: A watery layer on a gel-like food can result from syneresis: the structure contracts and releases some of the liquid it held. Yogurt and sour cream offer familiar examples. The liquid separation reflects a change within the gel, rather than proving that water was added afterward.

records.label: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial
records.learning_takeaway: Interpret a blood-pressure target comparison together with its enrollment limits and adverse effects.
records.card: SPRINT compared systolic-pressure targets below 120 and 140 mmHg in higher-risk adults aged fifty or older with initial systolic pressure at least 130 mmHg, excluding diabetes and prior stroke. Intensive treatment reduced cardiovascular events and deaths but increased some adverse effects; eligibility limits matter.

records.label: Tartini tone
records.learning_takeaway: Identify a difference tone produced by nonlinear interaction of two frequencies.
records.card: Two notes can give rise to an additional difference tone at the difference between their frequencies. Called a Tartini tone in music, it can result from nonlinear interactions in an instrument or the hearing system. The extra perceived pitch need not be one of the two notes originally played.

records.label: TCP congestion window
records.learning_takeaway: Limit unacknowledged sending with a network-congestion bound separate from the receiver's advertised capacity.
records.card: TCP's congestion window limits how much unacknowledged data a sender injects into the network. It is separate from the receiver's advertised window, which reflects receiver-side capacity. The smaller limit constrains sending, so available space at the receiver does not by itself justify faster transmission.

records.label: TCP slow start
records.learning_takeaway: Probe available network capacity by increasing outstanding data as acknowledgments arrive until a threshold or congestion intervenes.
records.card: TCP slow start probes how much data a connection can have outstanding by growing its congestion window as new data is acknowledged. Growth continues until a threshold or congestion changes the behavior. Despite its name, this phase can expand sending quickly rather than increasing by a fixed amount per round.

records.label: Tea as a British status good
records.learning_takeaway: Early expensive tea was guarded and consumed by elites; expanding imports helped transform it into a more widely accessible grocery.
records.card: Tea’s early expense in Britain made its storage and consumption a marker of status. Valuable supplies could be kept under lock. As imports expanded, tea became more widely available, showing how a once-exclusive luxury could become part of ordinary shopping and domestic routine.

records.label: Tellability
records.learning_takeaway: What makes a story worth telling depends on audience, situation and presentation, not merely whether events occurred.
records.card: Tellability asks what makes a story worth telling in a particular situation. An unusual event may help, but audience, context and presentation also matter. A sequence can qualify as a narrative yet fail to interest its listeners or give them a reason to care.

records.label: Temperature inversion
records.learning_takeaway: Explain how warmer air above cooler air can suppress mixing and trap near-surface pollution.
records.card: A temperature inversion occurs where air becomes warmer with height. Near the ground, warm air above cooler air can suppress mixing and trap pollution. Such inversions may form through nighttime surface cooling or warm-air advection above an existing cool layer.

records.label: Tennis racket dead spot
records.learning_takeaway: Understand an impact location where a stationary racket can absorb nearly all the ball's energy.
records.card: A ball dropped onto a suitably supported racket can stop almost dead after striking a particular location. Cross explains this through matching effective masses: the ball transfers its energy to the racket instead of rebounding strongly. The same location behaves differently when the racket is moving.

records.label: Tennis racket sweet spot
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish a low-vibration impact location from the point of maximum rebound speed.
records.card: Physicist Rod Cross distinguishes a tennis racket's vibration-node sweet spot from its center of percussion and point of fastest rebound. An impact at the vibration node removes that component of handle motion, but rotation and translation can still transmit forces to the hand.

records.label: Terminal velocity
records.learning_takeaway: A falling object stops accelerating when its increasing drag balances its effective downward force.
records.card: A falling object reaches terminal velocity when fluid resistance balances its effective downward force. Its speed then stops increasing even though gravity still acts. In the simple skydiver model, faster motion produces more drag until the net force and acceleration both become zero.

records.label: Terminus post quem
records.learning_takeaway: A deposit cannot predate its youngest securely associated object’s earliest possible date; this supplies a lower bound, not an exact deposition date.
records.card: A terminus post quem is an earliest possible date for a deposit or event. In archaeology, the most recently introduced securely associated artifact can supply that bound. An old coin may circulate for years, so its minting need not date burial exactly.

records.label: Terza rima
records.learning_takeaway: The middle rhyme of one tercet becomes the outer rhyme of the next, chaining stanzas forward.
records.card: Terza rima links three-line stanzas through interlocking rhyme: the middle rhyme of one stanza becomes the outer rhyme of the next. Each group thus reaches forward into another. The pattern creates continuity across stanza boundaries rather than treating every tercet as a closed unit.

records.label: Test–retest reliability
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish stability across repeated measurements from agreement among observers.
records.card: Test–retest reliability asks whether a measure produces consistent results across repeated administrations. It evaluates stability over occasions, whereas inter-rater reliability evaluates agreement among observers. A repeatable score can still measure the wrong thing, so consistency alone does not establish the validity of its interpretation.

records.label: The Ambassadors
records.learning_takeaway: Holbein’s double portrait joins the sitters and their objects with a distorted skull whose recognition depends on moving to an oblique viewpoint.
records.card: Holbein’s The Ambassadors presents two men with objects that invite close scrutiny, but a stretched skull disrupts the frontal view. Seen from an oblique position, the skull becomes recognizable. The painting makes a change in the viewer’s position part of encountering one of its key images.
records.primary_subfield: Works, movements and historical design cases

records.label: The New Coffee House trade token
records.learning_takeaway: A penny token from Exchange Alley advertised coffee, chocolate, tea and other goods while associating the shop with a Turkish ruler.
records.card: This penny token advertised a coffee house in London’s Exchange Alley through a list of goods and the image of a Turkish ruler. Coffee, chocolate and tea appeared together, showing how a small circulating object could advertise an establishment’s offerings and associations.

records.label: The Red Wheelbarrow
records.learning_takeaway: Williams splits compound words across short lines; an editorial reading interprets that lineation as shaping pacing and attention.
records.card: William Carlos Williams’s The Red Wheelbarrow breaks familiar compound words across short lines. An editorial reading treats those divisions as an invitation to slow down and attend to ordinary objects. The visible lineation supports that reading without making it the poem’s only possible effect.

records.label: Their Eyes Were Watching God
records.learning_takeaway: Janie’s retrospective telling to Pheoby frames a search for voice within a novel shaped by folklore and Black vernacular speech.
records.card: Janie recounts her life to Pheoby in Their Eyes Were Watching God, placing the novel’s events inside an act of retrospective telling. Hurston’s use of folklore and Black vernacular speech connects that structure with Janie’s developing voice and her struggle to speak for herself.

records.label: Thermocline
records.learning_takeaway: Recognize a depth interval where temperature drops rapidly below a warm mixed surface layer.
records.card: A thermocline is a layer where water temperature changes rapidly with depth, separating warmer surface water from colder water below. Its depth and strength vary with place and season. Recognizing the layer helps describe an ocean’s vertical structure instead of assuming its temperature is uniform.

records.label: Thermohaline circulation
records.learning_takeaway: Connect temperature and salinity differences with density-driven deep-ocean flow.
records.card: Temperature and salinity affect seawater density. In places where water becomes sufficiently cold and salty, it can sink and contribute to deep-ocean circulation, with other water moving to replace it. Thermohaline circulation highlights these density differences alongside the wind-driven motions visible at the surface.

records.label: Thermokarst
records.learning_takeaway: Use thaw-related ground subsidence to understand both lake formation and drainage.
records.card: When ice within the ground thaws, the land can subside and form thermokarst depressions. Some fill with lakes or ponds; elsewhere, thaw can breach a basin’s edge and drain a lake. Warming can therefore produce both expanding water bodies and abrupt losses of surface water.

records.label: Thin-film interference
records.learning_takeaway: Reflections at two film surfaces combine according to optical path length and reflection phase shifts.
records.card: Thin-film interference gives soap bubbles and oil films their changing colors. Light reflected from the film’s two boundaries travels different optical paths and may acquire different reflection phases. The waves then reinforce or cancel differently for different wavelengths, making thickness and surrounding materials matter.

records.label: Three-point bending test
records.learning_takeaway: Load a simply supported beam at its center to relate deflection to material and cross-section stiffness.
records.card: For a slender, uniform beam simply supported and loaded at its midpoint, an ideal three-point bending test links force and deflection. Linear-elastic, small-deflection beam theory predicts deflection proportional to load and span cubed, and inversely proportional to elastic modulus times second moment of area.

records.label: Threefold repetition
records.learning_takeaway: Explain the claimable three-occurrence draw procedure, including the timing of a claim before a qualifying intended move.
records.card: Under FIDE rules, threefold repetition permits a draw claim rather than automatically ending play. The player to move may claim when the position has appeared for the third time, or record an intended move producing it and declare that intention to the arbiter before moving.

records.label: Thrust vectoring
records.learning_takeaway: Deflect exhaust direction to change a vehicle’s thrust direction and maneuverability.
records.card: Thrust vectoring redirects an engine’s exhaust so the propulsive force can change direction. This gives a vehicle another way to maneuver rather than keeping thrust along one fixed axis. NASA describes rectangular nozzle exits as one design approach that makes the exhaust flow easier to deflect.

records.label: Tibetan mandala palace plan
records.learning_takeaway: A central palace and directional gates organize ritual space and the practitioner’s relation to the represented deity.
records.card: A Tibetan mandala can organize ritual space as a palace with a center and four directional gates. In the practitioner account described here, ritual objects occupy particular positions and the deity’s dwelling anchors orientation. The diagram therefore coordinates relationships rather than serving as decoration alone.

records.label: Tidal force
records.learning_takeaway: Differences in gravitational pull across an extended object create stretching and tidal effects.
records.card: Tidal forces arise because gravity differs across an extended object. The side nearer an attracting body is pulled more strongly than the far side. Comparing each part’s acceleration with the object’s center explains stretching, ocean-tide patterns, and potentially the disruption of stars passing too close.

records.label: Tidal locking
records.learning_takeaway: Dissipative tidal deformation can synchronize an orbiting body’s spin with its orbital motion.
records.card: Tidal locking synchronizes a body’s rotation with its orbital motion through long-term tidal interactions and dissipation. Earth’s Moon therefore keeps roughly the same face toward Earth while still rotating. The fixed-looking lunar face reflects matched rotation and orbital periods, not absence of spin.

records.label: Timar
records.learning_takeaway: A revocable right to collect revenue supported Ottoman service personnel without making their assignments automatically hereditary.
records.card: An Ottoman timar granted the right to collect revenue from a specified area in return for service. It supported its holder without a regular state salary. Because the grant could be revoked and did not automatically pass to heirs, it also limited independent hereditary power.

records.label: Titration end point and equivalence point
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish an observed end-point signal from the exact stoichiometric equivalence condition.
records.card: A titration’s equivalence point is the exact stoichiometric condition where the reacting amounts match the equation. Its end point is the observed signal used to stop measuring, such as a color change. A good method makes the difference between these two points small.

records.label: TLS 1.3
records.learning_takeaway: Negotiate authenticated encrypted channels using a redesigned handshake that removes static public-key key exchange.
records.card: TLS 1.3 is a protocol for establishing authenticated, encrypted communication. Its redesign removed static RSA and static Diffie–Hellman key exchange, so its public-key exchange modes provide forward secrecy. Other modes have different properties, and early data requires particular care about replay and weaker security guarantees.

records.label: Tonal answer in fugue
records.learning_takeaway: Understand why a fugue answer alters intervals to navigate tonic and dominant.
records.card: A fugue's answer is a subject entry associated with the dominant key. In a tonal answer, some intervals are changed to accommodate the movement between tonic and dominant. A real answer instead preserves the intervals, making tonal function and literal transposition different possible priorities.

records.label: Torque-induced gyroscopic precession
records.learning_takeaway: A perpendicular torque changes a spinning object’s angular-momentum direction instead of simply tipping it over.
records.card: When a rapidly spinning gyroscope experiences a torque perpendicular to its angular momentum, that vector turns rather than simply shrinking. In the slow-precession approximation, precession is much slower than the disk’s spin. This model explains a tilted top’s steady turning around the vertical.

records.label: Torus
records.learning_takeaway: Gluing opposite rectangle edges without twists creates a genus-one surface and models two periodic coordinates.
records.card: An ordinary torus is a surface with one handle, often pictured as a doughnut. It can also be constructed by identifying opposite edges of a rectangle without twists. This edge-gluing description makes the surface useful for representing two independently periodic coordinates.

records.label: Total impulse
records.learning_takeaway: Integrate thrust over firing time to measure a propulsion system’s accumulated momentum delivery.
records.card: Total impulse accumulates thrust over the duration of a burn. For constant thrust it is force multiplied by time; for varying thrust it is the area under the thrust–time curve. Engines with the same peak thrust can therefore deliver different total impulses if their firing histories differ.

records.label: Total internal reflection
records.learning_takeaway: Above the critical angle, light entering a lower-index boundary reflects back instead of transmitting.
records.card: At an ideal nonabsorbing interface, total internal reflection occurs toward a lower-index medium at an incidence angle beyond the critical angle. Instead of a propagating refracted ray emerging, light is reflected back. The index ordering matters: increasing the angle at an arbitrary boundary is insufficient.

records.label: Touch-move rule
records.learning_takeaway: Understand how deliberate touching commits a player when a legal move exists.
records.card: In over-the-board chess, a player whose turn it is normally must move the first deliberately touched own piece that has a legal move. Announcing an intention to adjust a piece before touching it is different. Clearly accidental contact does not count as deliberate selection.

records.label: Toyota Motor Corporation
records.learning_takeaway: See how the company's production system joins abnormality detection with demand-coordinated flow rather than optimizing only machine speed.
records.card: Toyota's official production-system account combines just-in-time flow with jidoka, the practice of responding to abnormalities. One coordinates when work and parts are needed; the other helps prevent defects from continuing unnoticed. The case presents production as linked processes, rather than equating productivity only with machines running faster.
records.primary_subfield: Economic history and documented business cases

records.label: Track circuit
records.learning_takeaway: A train shunts an electrical rail circuit so the signalling system detects occupied track.
records.card: A track circuit uses the rails as part of an electrical path to detect whether a railway section is clear. In a basic relay-based arrangement, a train shunts current away from the relay. The wider signalling system uses this indication when deciding whether another train may proceed.
records.primary_subfield: Transport systems and engineered case studies

records.label: Transhumance
records.learning_takeaway: Seasonal movement between different pastures links otherwise separate places into a recurring system of herding and habitation.
records.card: Transhumance moves herds and herders between seasonally useful pastures. A mountain summer grazing area and a lowland winter area function together through the route connecting them. Following that annual movement reveals a landscape organized around recurring mobility rather than one permanently occupied settlement.

records.label: Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite
records.learning_takeaway: An all-sky survey of bright stars makes transit discoveries practical targets for follow-up characterization.
records.card: TESS was designed to search bright stars across the sky for periodic dimming caused by planetary transits. Bright host stars make promising candidates easier to examine with other telescopes. Its survey strategy connects planet detection with follow-up studies of planetary masses, compositions, and atmospheres.

records.label: Transition-relevance place
records.learning_takeaway: Recognize a possible completion point where another speaker may take over, although the current speaker can continue.
records.card: A transition-relevance place is a point where a conversational turn could be complete and speaker change becomes possible. The current speaker may select someone, another participant may begin, or the speaker may continue. It is an opportunity for transition, rather than an automatic instruction that the turn must end.

records.label: Trap cropping
records.learning_takeaway: Redirect a pest toward a more attractive planting, while checking that the arrangement works for that pest and crop.
records.card: Trap cropping uses a more attractive planting to draw pests away from the crop being protected. The result depends on the pest, the plants and their arrangement. Extension examples include useful flea-beetle diversion and unsuccessful combinations, showing why companion-planting claims need evidence for the particular situation.

records.label: Travel-time service area
records.learning_takeaway: A reachable area follows network paths and travel costs, so it need not match a circle drawn at a fixed distance.
records.card: A travel-time service area shows locations reachable through a network within a specified travel cost. Roads, connections and restrictions shape its boundary, so it need not resemble a circle. The result describes accessibility under the model’s assumptions rather than simple straight-line proximity.

records.label: Triad (social group)
records.learning_takeaway: See how adding a third member permits coalitions and lets the group persist after one member leaves.
records.card: A triad is a three-person social group. Adding the third member creates possibilities unavailable in a dyad, including two-against-one coalitions and a majority view. If someone withdraws, the remaining pair can still interact, so the group's relationships are not all dependent on one uninterrupted two-person bond.

records.label: Triadic closure
records.learning_takeaway: Understand why two people sharing a friend are more likely to form a connection, without treating this as inevitable.
records.card: Triadic closure is the tendency for two people with a shared friend to become connected themselves. Meeting opportunities and social context can help such ties form. It is a pattern of network development, not a guarantee that every pair of friends-of-friends will eventually know each other.

records.label: Triple point
records.learning_takeaway: Three phases coexist at one pressure-temperature combination on a pure-substance phase diagram.
records.card: A pure substance’s triple point is the pressure and temperature where three phases coexist in equilibrium. On water’s phase diagram, it is where the solid–liquid, liquid–vapor, and solid–vapor boundaries meet. Below that pressure, liquid water is not an equilibrium phase.

records.label: Trompe-l’oeil
records.learning_takeaway: Trompe-l’oeil pictures an object so deceptively that viewers may take the painted representation for the object itself.
records.card: Trompe-l’oeil aims to make a painted representation appear to be the object itself. The term describes a potential illusion rather than realism alone: a viewer may momentarily mistake a depicted object for something physically present.

records.label: Tubuloglomerular feedback
records.learning_takeaway: Trace tubular salt delivery to local changes in afferent-arteriole resistance.
records.card: Cells along a kidney tubule sense changes in the fluid and salt reaching them. Their local signals adjust resistance in the arteriole feeding the filter. Tubuloglomerular feedback therefore uses information downstream of filtration to help regulate how much new fluid is filtered.

records.label: Tudor London cookshops
records.learning_takeaway: Commercial ovens supplied hot ready-made food to city residents whose cramped homes lacked cooking facilities.
records.card: Tudor Londoners could buy prepared hot food from cookshops, especially when cramped homes lacked cooking facilities. Commercial ovens supplied ready-to-eat meals outside the household. The museum notes that evidence about the exact meals and their customers is limited, preserving uncertainty alongside the practical explanation.

records.label: Turbidity
records.learning_takeaway: Connect suspended matter with light scattering, absorption and reduced underwater visibility.
records.card: Turbidity describes water cloudiness associated with suspended particles and other material that interferes with light. Sediment or algae can reduce visibility and the light reaching underwater plants. Cloudy water is not automatically polluted, since some waters are naturally turbid, but the change can still matter ecologically.

records.label: Twenty Squares
records.learning_takeaway: Explore how an imported ancient game acquired Egyptian markings and visual conventions.
records.card: Twenty Squares spread across the ancient Near East and was later imported into Egypt. Surviving boards reveal adaptation rather than simple copying: special squares on Near Eastern examples display rosettes, while Egyptian examples use hieroglyphs. A shared game could acquire a different visual language.

records.label: Two Pages
records.learning_takeaway: Explore Glass's additive process through repetitions that successively omit final notes.
records.card: At the opening of Philip Glass's Two Pages, growth comes from adding repetitions whose final notes are progressively removed. A motive can therefore expand while newly added units become shorter. The cited analysis illustrates how repetition and subtraction can cooperate within an additive process.

records.label: Two truths in Indian Buddhist philosophy
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish conventional and ultimate truth while recognizing that Buddhist schools interpret the distinction differently.
records.card: Indian Buddhist discussions of two truths distinguish conventional understanding from an ultimate perspective. Ordinary language and practices operate conventionally, while ultimate analysis asks how things really are. Buddhist schools interpret both levels and their relationship differently, so the distinction does not express one uniform doctrine across traditions.

records.label: Tympanometry
records.learning_takeaway: Assess middle-ear mechanics by measuring eardrum movement as pressure changes.
records.card: Tympanometry changes air pressure in the ear canal and records how the eardrum responds. The resulting graph helps assess the mechanics of the eardrum and middle ear. It differs from asking someone whether they can hear a tone: movement and hearing threshold are separate measurements.

records.label: Uncodified constitution
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish lacking a single constitutional document from lacking written constitutional rules.
records.card: An uncodified constitution lacks one consolidated constitutional text, not necessarily written rules. The United Kingdom's constitutional arrangements include many statutes alongside other sources. Calling the constitution unwritten can therefore mislead: the important distinction is whether its basic rules are collected in a single authoritative document.

records.label: Underpromotion
records.learning_takeaway: Recognize that promotion may choose a rook, bishop or knight instead of queen.
records.card: A pawn reaching its final rank need not become a queen. Underpromotion chooses a rook, bishop or knight instead. The new piece takes effect immediately, and the available choices do not depend on which pieces were captured earlier in the game.

records.label: Understitching
records.learning_takeaway: Keep a facing from rolling to the garment’s outside by securing its seam allowance to the facing.
records.card: Understitching secures a seam allowance to the facing on the inside of a garment. This encourages the seam to roll inward and helps prevent the facing from showing on the outside. It controls an already assembled edge, rather than stabilizing a loose pattern piece before sewing.

records.label: Unicode code point
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish the integer assigned to a character from the bytes used by an encoding.
records.card: A Unicode code point is a numbered position in the character space, rather than the bytes stored in a file. UTF-8 encodes valid scalar values with different byte lengths. Keeping the number separate from its encoding helps explain why counting bytes need not count characters.

records.label: Unicode normalization
records.learning_takeaway: Transform equivalent character sequences into a common binary representation through decomposition, ordering, and optional recomposition.
records.card: Unicode normalization gives equivalent text sequences a common representation. It decomposes characters, orders combining marks, and sometimes recomposes them. The chosen normalization form matters: canonical forms preserve distinctions that compatibility forms may remove, so normalization is more specific than simply making text look alike.

records.label: Unit cell
records.learning_takeaway: Account for shared boundary atoms when identifying the repeating building block of a crystal.
records.card: A unit cell is a repeating box used to describe a crystal lattice. Boundary points are shared with neighboring cells, so counting them requires fractions. A primitive cell contains one lattice point in total; a larger, nonprimitive cell contains more.

records.label: Unreliable narration
records.learning_takeaway: A narrator may report events accurately while interpreting or evaluating them misleadingly, so unreliability need not mean simple lying.
records.card: A narrator can report events accurately yet interpret them poorly or evaluate them misleadingly. Unreliable narration therefore involves more than factual lying. Separating reporting, interpretation and judgment lets readers identify where an account becomes questionable and where it may remain dependable.

records.label: UTF-8
records.learning_takeaway: Encode Unicode scalar values in one to four bytes while preserving ASCII byte values.
records.card: UTF-8 represents Unicode scalar values using one to four bytes. ASCII characters retain their familiar single-byte values, while other values use recognizable multibyte patterns. A character's assigned number and its encoded bytes are different things, which matters when counting or processing text.

records.label: Value-added theory of collective behavior
records.learning_takeaway: Analyze several proposed conditions for collective episodes, including strain, shared beliefs, and precipitating events.
records.card: Smelser's value-added theory analyzes collective behavior through a proposed combination of conditions, including structural strain, a shared interpretation, and a precipitating event. It asks what makes an episode possible and mobilizes action. The name refers to an explanatory sociological framework, rather than economic value added or a numerical prediction formula.

records.label: Variable-area exhaust nozzle
records.learning_takeaway: Adjustable nozzle geometry trades extra weight for efficient operation across a wider airflow range.
records.card: A variable-area exhaust nozzle changes geometry to suit different engine operating conditions. Afterburning jet engines use adjustable converging-diverging passages to maintain useful flow conditions over a wider range. The moving structure adds weight, revealing a tradeoff between adaptable performance and the simplicity of a fixed nozzle.

records.label: Variable expressivity
records.learning_takeaway: Distinguish variation in a condition’s manifestations from whether it appears at all.
records.card: People with the same genetic condition can have different signs, symptoms or severity. Variable expressivity describes that range of manifestations. It differs from reduced penetrance, which concerns whether the condition appears at all, and helps explain why affected relatives need not look clinically identical.

records.label: Variable-rate irrigation
records.learning_takeaway: Match irrigation amounts to different areas of a field instead of assuming every area needs the same water.
records.card: Variable-rate irrigation changes water delivery across a field using control zones and prescription maps. Those maps specify irrigation amounts, but soil and crop information must guide the prescription. The technology applies the planned pattern; it does not independently determine how much water a crop needs.

records.label: Variationist sociolinguistics
records.learning_takeaway: Analyze how linguistic and social conditions alter the probability of variants in language as actually used.
records.card: Variationist sociolinguistics studies language as people use it, asking how social settings and linguistic environments influence variation. Instead of imagining one perfectly uniform speaker, it examines patterns across actual speech. A person may use the same variant at different rates when chatting casually and reading aloud.

records.label: Venice and its lagoon
records.learning_takeaway: Island settlements and canals form an urban system inseparable from the surrounding lagoon and centuries of hydraulic intervention.
records.card: Venice developed as an urban system of islands and waterways within a lagoon. Buildings, canals and hydraulic interventions cannot be understood independently of that surrounding water. The site shows a city whose form emerged through a long, changing relationship between settlement and environmental management.

records.label: Villa Savoye
records.learning_takeaway: The villa demonstrates how columns and floor slabs can separate structure from wall placement, enabling a free plan and an independently organized facade.
records.card: Villa Savoye demonstrates how columns and floor slabs can separate a building’s structural support from the placement of walls. This permits a free plan and an independently arranged facade. The villa makes a design program visible through the relationships among support, enclosure and inhabited space.
records.primary_subfield: Works, movements and historical design cases

records.label: Villanelle
records.learning_takeaway: Two refrains alternate through five tercets and join in a final quatrain, letting recurring words acquire different force.
records.card: A villanelle uses five three-line stanzas and a final four-line stanza, with two alternating refrains that come together at the end. Repetition provides a stable structure, while the surrounding lines can change how each returning phrase is heard or understood.

records.label: Virginia Apgar
records.learning_takeaway: See how a rapid standardized assessment made newborn condition more consistently observable.
records.card: Virginia Apgar developed a standardized way to assess a newborn soon after birth. Observations of heart rate, breathing effort, muscle tone, reflex response and color were combined into one score. Her work turned several immediate clinical observations into a repeatable assessment of the transition outside the womb.

records.label: Virtual organization
records.learning_takeaway: Coordinate geographically dispersed expertise and outsourced activities through communication technologies, with trust and isolation challenges.
records.card: A virtual organization uses communication technologies to connect dispersed expertise and activities beyond a single stable workplace. It can draw on remote teams or outsourced functions. The flexibility also creates coordination problems: limited interaction may weaken trust and leave participants feeling isolated from colleagues or the organization.

records.label: Volcano ground-deformation monitoring
records.learning_takeaway: Infer subsurface magma changes from repeated measurements of surface movement.
records.card: A volcano’s surface can move as conditions change below it. Repeated GPS positions and tilt measurements help researchers infer changes in a magma reservoir’s depth or volume. Monitoring deformation turns small surface shifts into clues about an inaccessible system, while still requiring interpretation alongside other evidence.

records.label: Vulnerability in bridge
records.learning_takeaway: See how increased bonuses and penalties change a contract's stakes.
records.card: Vulnerability changes bridge's rewards and risks: successful contracts can earn higher bonuses, while failed contracts can incur greater penalties. In duplicate bridge, the board determines which partnership is vulnerable. This differs from rubber bridge, where winning a game changes a partnership's vulnerability.

records.label: WAL checkpointing
records.learning_takeaway: In SQLite, move committed log content into the database as a separate operation from reading, writing, and committing.
records.card: In SQLite, a WAL checkpoint transfers committed changes from the write-ahead log into the main database file. It is separate from reading, writing, or committing a transaction. SQLite can schedule checkpoints automatically or let applications control when they run to manage the accumulated log.

records.label: Walden
records.learning_takeaway: Thoreau’s account of life by Walden Pond invites an editorial reading of withdrawal from conventional society as an experiment in ways of living.
records.card: Walden recounts Thoreau’s time living by Walden Pond and has inspired readers to reconsider conventional society. An editorial reading treats the account as an experiment in ways of living. That interpretation invites reflection without claiming to establish why the book’s influence has endured.

records.label: Wandle textile design
records.learning_takeaway: Wandle’s repeat measures 98.4 by 44.5 centimeters; the V&A identifies it as the largest Morris attempted.
records.card: William Morris’s Wandle has a pattern repeat measuring 98.4 by 44.5 centimeters, which the V&A calls his largest attempt. An editorial comparison asks how such a large repeating unit shapes a fabric’s composition beyond the scale of its individual motifs.
records.primary_subfield: Works, movements and historical design cases

records.label: Warp tension
records.learning_takeaway: Balance a warp firmly enough to form the shed without unnecessarily straining the yarn and loom.
records.card: Warp threads need suitable, reasonably even tension while weaving. On a rigid-heddle loom, too little can let the raised reed fall, while too much can make changing positions difficult and strain the yarn. Good control means balancing the working tension, not simply making every thread as tight as possible.

records.label: Warranties as quality assurance
records.learning_takeaway: Shift specified repair or replacement obligations to a seller so buyers need not verify every quality claim beforehand.
records.card: A warranty promises specified repair or replacement if a product fails within agreed conditions. It reduces the need for buyers to verify every aspect of quality before purchase by assigning some consequences to the seller. Its protection depends on the actual terms, rather than the label alone.

records.label: Washout periods in crossover trials
records.learning_takeaway: Explain why effects from one treatment period can contaminate the next comparison.
records.card: In a crossover study, the effects of one treatment period can persist into the next. A washout period leaves time without the intervention so those effects can diminish. Its usefulness depends on how long effects last; an arbitrary pause does not guarantee an uncontaminated comparison.

records.label: We Real Cool
records.learning_takeaway: Brooks places a collective pronoun at line endings; an editorial reading connects the recurring group voice with the poem’s final reference to death.
records.card: In We Real Cool, Gwendolyn Brooks repeatedly places the collective pronoun at line endings before the poem’s final reference to death. An editorial reading hears group bravado meeting a sudden limit. The formal pattern makes the relation between a shared voice and its ending available for interpretation.

records.label: Weak ties
records.learning_takeaway: See why acquaintances can connect people to information outside densely connected close-friend circles.
records.card: Weak ties are less-close relationships, such as acquaintances, that may connect someone to information outside their usual circle. Close friends often know many of the same people. An acquaintance can therefore provide a different route, although a tie's usefulness depends on its network position rather than weakness alone.

records.label: Western Christian monasticism
records.learning_takeaway: Withdrawal into disciplined religious life could take solitary or communal forms and also sustain learning, hospitality and artistic work.
records.card: Western Christian monasticism organized disciplined religious life through withdrawal from ordinary worldly pursuits. It could take solitary or communal forms, while monasteries also provided hospitality, learning and artistic production. Withdrawal therefore did not necessarily mean a complete absence of relationships with surrounding society.

records.label: William Labov
records.learning_takeaway: See how occupation, education, and income were used to compare linguistic variant frequencies across social strata.
records.card: William Labov's study of New York speech compared linguistic variation with occupation, education, and income. It also examined differences between casual speech and reading. The case shows how social categories become research variables and why contextual variation must be considered alongside differences between groups.

records.label: Wind-instrument end correction
records.learning_takeaway: Understand why an open pipe resonates as though it were slightly longer.
records.card: An open pipe behaves acoustically as though it extends slightly beyond its physical opening.
