The air's motion spreads outward before the pressure reflection develops, increasing the effective vibrating length. A resonance therefore occurs slightly lower than a simple model using only the measured tube length predicts.

records.label: Winner's curse
records.learning_takeaway: Condition an estimate on winning because the highest bid may reveal an unusually optimistic initial estimate.
records.card: The winner's curse can occur when the highest bidder also has an unusually high estimate of a shared uncertain value. Winning provides information about how optimistic that estimate was relative to others. Accounting for this selection before bidding differs from simply paying what one's initial estimate suggested.

records.label: Wood sorption hysteresis
records.learning_takeaway: Understand why wood’s moisture history can matter even at the same temperature and relative humidity.
records.card: Wood’s equilibrium moisture content can depend on whether it reached a humidity level by drying or by absorbing water. At the same temperature and relative humidity, the drying path can retain more moisture. This sorption hysteresis makes moisture history relevant even after equilibrium is reached.

records.label: Worked example
records.learning_takeaway: Study a demonstrated solution path before attempting comparable problems, especially while building initial expertise.
records.card: A worked example shows a solution path rather than asking a beginner to discover every step unaided. Studying examples alongside similar problems can focus attention on how the procedure works. The IES guide also notes that the appropriate amount of guidance changes as learners develop greater expertise.

records.label: Working memory model
records.learning_takeaway: Explore a model that separates temporary verbal and visual-spatial processing under executive control.
records.card: Baddeley and Hitch's working-memory model treats temporary mental activity as more than a single storage box. A central executive coordinates specialized systems for verbal and visual-spatial material. The later addition of an episodic buffer illustrates that this is a developing explanatory model, not an immutable anatomical diagram.

records.label: Write-ahead logging
records.learning_takeaway: See how SQLite's WAL mode appends changes separately before checkpointing them into the main database, allowing concurrent readers.
records.card: In SQLite's write-ahead-log mode, changes are appended to a separate log instead of immediately overwriting the main database file. A commit record marks completion, and readers can continue using an earlier view. Later checkpointing moves committed changes back into the database.

records.label: Wudu
records.learning_takeaway: Ritual washing prepares worshippers for salat, linking bodily preparation with the formal transition into prayer.
records.card: Wudu is ritual washing associated with preparation for Muslim prayer. It belongs to the sequence leading into salat rather than functioning only as ordinary cleaning. An editorial comparison can consider how this bodily preparation marks the transition into formal prayer.

records.label: XMM-Newton
records.learning_takeaway: Nested grazing-incidence mirrors focus X-rays while separate instruments collect complementary spectra and optical data.
records.card: XMM-Newton focuses X-rays with nested mirrors struck at shallow grazing angles. Each of its three mirror modules contains fifty-eight shells, increasing the collecting surface in a compact assembly. Additional instruments separate X-ray wavelengths and observe optical and ultraviolet light, giving complementary information about the same targets.

records.label: Yerkes–Dodson relationship
records.learning_takeaway: Investigate why task difficulty matters when relating arousal to performance.
records.card: The Yerkes–Dodson relationship links arousal and performance while emphasizing task difficulty. A demanding task may be disrupted at an arousal level that suits a simple one. The useful lesson is not that moderate arousal always wins, but that an apparent optimum depends on the task.

records.label: Young’s modulus
records.learning_takeaway: Compare axial stiffness through the stress-to-strain ratio within a material’s linear elastic range.
records.card: Young’s modulus measures how much axial stress is needed to produce a given strain within a material’s linear elastic range. A larger value means greater stiffness, not necessarily a higher failure stress. The distinction helps separate resistance to small deformation from the limits of safe loading.

records.label: Zero-force truss member
records.learning_takeaway: Joint geometry and loading can identify members carrying no axial force for the specific load case.
records.card: In an ideal truss, a member can carry zero axial force under a particular load. At an unloaded joint with three members, if exactly two are collinear, the third is unloaded. It may still brace other members or carry force when the loading changes.

records.label: Zero-order reaction kinetics
records.learning_takeaway: Under specified conditions a reaction rate can remain concentration-independent until those conditions cease.
records.card: A zero-order reaction consumes reactant at a constant rate over the conditions where its rate law applies. Increasing that reactant’s concentration does not speed the reaction. This cannot continue after the reactant is exhausted, so the constant-rate behavior has a limited operating range.

records.label: Zeugma
records.learning_takeaway: One governing word serves multiple parts of a sentence, linking them through shared grammar rather than repeating the word.
records.card: Zeugma uses one governing word to serve several parts of a sentence. Shared grammar links the elements without repeating that word. Some examples exploit different senses for wit, but the broader device does not require every instance to turn on a semantic joke.

records.label: Zheng He’s maritime expeditions
records.learning_takeaway: Ming fleets projected imperial prestige and carried envoys through Indian Ocean networks rather than simply opening an unknown sea route.
records.card: Zheng He’s Ming fleets traveled through established Indian Ocean networks carrying envoys and projecting imperial prestige. Their journeys connected diplomacy, trade and demonstrations of power. Understanding those purposes shifts attention from a simple story of discovering unknown places to the political relationships the voyages sought to organize.

records.label: Zhuangzi’s butterfly dream
records.learning_takeaway: Examine whether feeling awake guarantees a final, privileged perspective on experience.
records.card: Zhuangzi's butterfly dream reverses the security of waking identity: was Zhuangzi dreaming of a butterfly, or is a butterfly dreaming of Zhuangzi? In the cited interpretation, the story encourages modesty about one's present perspective. Feeling released from an earlier error need not establish a final standpoint.

records.label: Zone refining
records.learning_takeaway: A moving molten zone carries impurities toward the end of a silicon rod for removal.
records.card: Zone refining purifies silicon by moving a narrow molten region along a solid rod. Impurities more soluble in the melt travel with that moving zone. Removing an impurity-rich end improves the material’s purity, supporting the preparation of silicon for semiconductor manufacture.

records.label: Zora Neale Hurston
records.learning_takeaway: Hurston transformed lived experience, including a hurricane, into fiction while insisting on the value of Black folklore and idiom.
records.card: Zora Neale Hurston brought her commitment to Black folklore and everyday speech into fiction. In Their Eyes Were Watching God, she also transformed experiences from her life, including surviving a hurricane. The connection shows how lived experience can become literary material without making a novel an autobiography.
